_source.text: 108. WILLIAM FINLAY was indicted for stealing, on the 10th of November , 1 hat, value 9s. , the goods of Henry Heath . THOMAS COLE . I live with Mr. Henry Heath, a hatter, in Oxford-street. I did not see this hat taken, but shortly after seven o'clock in the evening of the 10th of November, I missed it from inside the door - I was thinking what my employer might say when a Policeman came; I found it at Bow-street. WILLIAM McDONALD . I am a Police-constable. I took the prisoner, offering this hat
_source.title: WILLIAM FINLAY. Theft; simple larceny (from 1827). 1st December 1831.

_source.text: Before Mr. Justice Littledale. 125. JOHN WEBB was indicted for feloniously killing and slaying Thomas Fordham . JAMES WESTWOOD . I am coachman to Mr. Biggs, a stable-keeper, South-place, Finsbury . Thomas Fordham was his ostler - the prisoner is a coachman in Mr. Bigg's employ. On Saturday, the 29th of October, I saw Webb and Fordham in the yard in South-place - I heard Fordham say, in the middle of the day, that Webb was a twofaced fellow, and something more which he could tell him, but what he
_source.title: JOHN WEBB. Killing; manslaughter. 1st December 1831.

text: the prisoner the day before? A. I cannot say. CHARLES ROBARTS . I am a <mark>surgeon</mark>. I was called to see the deceased on Saturday evening, the 29th of October; he was then dying - I saw him after he was dead; he died at his own house - I examined his head, and found an extravasation of blood over the

- I do not think the blow would have caused his death if he had been sober. WILLIAM FINER . I am a district <mark>surgeon</mark> of Shoreditch. I examined the deceased - his death was caused by a large coagulum of blood on the left hemisphere of the brain, occasioned by the blow or fall. GUILTY . Aged 31. - Fined 1s. and Discharged.

_source.text: 130. JOHN SEAL was indicted for stealing, on the 9th of November , 1 gold pin, set with pearls, value 5s., the goods of James Gadsden , from his person . JAMES GADSDEN . I live in Furnival's Inn, and am a solicitor . On the 9th of November, about three o'clock in the afternoon, I was in Cheapside : my gold pin, set with pearls was in my stock; there was a very great crowd - I was walking in the middle of the road, to avoid the crowd - two or three people were round me; the prisoner came up to me
_source.title: JOHN SEAL. Theft; pocketpicking. 1st December 1831.
